title: Sympathetic vs parasympathetic
objective: Contrast the sympathetic and parasympathetic branches by their roles and outflow.

steps.title: Two branches, opposite leanings
steps.body:
The [[autonomic nervous system]] has two motor branches:

- **[[sympathetic]]** — mobilizes the body ('fight or flight'); outflow from thoracic and upper-lumbar cord.
- **[[parasympathetic]]** — supports rest and digestion; outflow from the brainstem (including the [[vagus nerve]]) and sacral cord.

Most organs get both and sit at a balance point between them.

steps.prompt: Match the branch to its lean.
steps.explanation: They're not strictly on/off opposites, but the 'mobilize vs restore' framing captures the usual balance.

steps.prompt: The vagus nerve is a major component of which branch?
steps.explanation: The vagus is the body's main parasympathetic nerve. (Its SENSORY fibers, with cell bodies in the nodose ganglion, are a separate story — covered in D2-L3.)

variants.setup: The vagus nerve is a major visceral nerve.
variants.prompt: Which division of the nervous system is it a major component of?
variants.reveal: The vagus is the main parasympathetic nerve to the viscera; its sensory fibers (cell bodies in the nodose ganglion) carry much interoception.
